paragraphs: Rabbi Eliezer or Rabbi Elazar is usually called Rabbi Liezer in the Jerusalem Talmud, following its practice of dropping an initial letter; similarly, amar, “said,” is mar in the Jerusalem Talmud, and so on.[^1][^2]

notes.text: בשם here means “by the name,” not that Liezer reports another scholar. The example is the shortening of amar to mar. The source’s grammatical היא remains unchanged.

The notice gives Hyman’s explanation of Liezer as a shortened name form. It does not establish that every occurrence of Eliezer and Elazar names the same person, or supply a count of occurrences throughout the literature.
